Usage: agentcage cage update [OPTIONS] [NAME]

  Rebuild and restart an existing cage.

  NAME is optional when ``-c`` is given — the cage to update is taken from the
  config's ``name:`` field. Mirrors ``cage create``, which has never required a
  positional NAME for the same reason.

  When the cage's inputs are unchanged and it is running, update asks the
  registry whether a base image has moved (`podman manifest inspect`, no layers
  are pulled): the egress image's and the cage image's `FROM` references, or
  the cage image itself when it is not built. If one has, that image is rebuilt
  (or re-pulled), and the cage restarts only if the rebuilt image differs from
  the one it is running. If the registry cannot be reached, update warns and
  treats the bases as unchanged. --no-pull skips the check.

  On the apple-container backend there is no registry check: the `container`
  CLI cannot read a remote digest without pulling, so the cage image's upstream
  references are pulled as before, and the shared egress image is rebuilt only
  with --pull or --no-cache.

Options:
  -c, --config PATH
  --no-cache         Force a full image rebuild (ignore podman's layer cache).
                     Use after pulling a fresh agentcage release that changed
                     the Containerfile or any of its build context.
  --pull             Force re-pull of the base image from the registry
                     (--pull=always). Combine with --no-cache for a fully clean
                     rebuild.
  --no-pull          Do not ask the registry whether a base image moved; only
                     changed inputs, --force or --no-cache rebuild. For offline
                     use, or to keep the images fixed.
  --force            Rebuild and restart even when inputs are unchanged.
  --no-color         Disable colored output.
  --quiet            Suppress progress output (spinners and banners).
  -h, --help         Show this message and exit.
